# Part 2: Books to Scrape

<https://books.toscrape.com>

A fake bookstore built for practicing web scraping. Use SelectorGadget (or view the page source) to explore the page.

```{r}
books_page <- read_html("https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/page-1.html")
```

Each book is an `<article class="product_pod">`. Fill in the blanks to scrape the title, price, and rating:

```{r}
#| eval: false
cards <- books_page |>
  html_elements("article.product_pod")

# the full title is in the `title` attribute of the link inside the <h3>
_______ <- cards |>
  html_element("h3 a") |>
  html_attr("title")

# the price is the text of an element with class `price_color`
_______ <- cards |>
  html_element(".price_color") |>
  html_text()

# the rating is stored in the *class* of the element with class `star-rating`
_______ <- cards |>
  html_element(".star-rating") |>
  html_attr("class")

books <- tibble(
  
)

books
```

# Save your data

For a bigger scraping project, you'd run the scraping code **once**, in an R script, and save the result so that you don't need to scrape again.

Create a new R script called `scrape-books.R`. Put your `scrape_books` function and the code that scrapes pages 1-3 in it, and finish with:

# If a site doesn't allow scraping

IMDb's Top 250 movies is a classic scraping example, but IMDb does not allow scraping:

```{r}
paths_allowed("https://www.imdb.com/chart/top")
```

What would you do if you wanted to analyze IMDb ratings? List at least two alternatives.
